question: What critical assessment must a nurse make before administering ear drops?

options.A: Check the patient's blood pressure and pulse
options.B: Confirm that the eardrum is intact
options.C: Test the patient's hearing using a tuning fork
options.D: Measure the exact width of the ear canal

explanation: Putting drops into an ear with a ruptured eardrum can cause severe pain and push infection deeper into the inner ear. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h4)

question: What is the main goal of respecting patient autonomy in end-of-life care?

options.A: Reducing the workload of the attending nursing staff
options.B: Ensuring family members make all major medical decisions
options.C: Allowing the patient to keep control over their choices
options.D: Speeding up the discharge process from the facility

explanation: Respecting autonomy means empowering the patient to direct their own care and make meaningful decisions about their remaining time. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h2)

question: A manager promises extra pay for extra shifts, but staff know management never pays up. Which part of Vroom's theory is broken?

options.A: Hygiene factor
options.B: Expectancy
options.C: Instrumentality
options.D: Valence

explanation: You got it! Instrumentality is the link between doing a good job and actually getting the promised reward. If staff don't trust management, that link is broken.

question: What does Gross National Product (GNP) measure?

options.A: The total amount of physical cash printed by the central bank
options.B: Only the money earned by foreign companies inside the country
options.C: The total cost of running public hospitals for one year
options.D: The total economic value produced by a country's citizens globally

explanation: Think of GNP as tracking the wealth created by a country's people, no matter where in the world they are working! You've got this.

question: Which of these is NOT a safe data security practice for a clinical nurse?

options.A: Leaving an active patient chart open on the screen while walking away
options.B: Keeping personal computer login passwords private and confidential
options.C: Logging out of the electronic health record station before taking a break
options.D: Reporting unfamiliar software pop-ups to the hospital IT department

explanation: Never leave an unattended terminal logged in! It allows unauthorized eyes to see or change confidential patient information. Always lock your screen. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which ethical principle refers to the nurse's core duty to do no harm to patients?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Justice
options.C: Non-maleficence
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Great nursing foundation here! 'Non-maleficence' literally means avoiding any physical, emotional, or psychological harm to the patients in your care.

question: What tool do Nigerian nurses commonly use in local clinics to track a child's growth and immunization records?

options.A: Cardiovascular risk profile
options.B: Intensive care flow sheet
options.C: Surgical safety checklist
options.D: National Child Health Card

explanation: Correct! The Child Health Card has the WHO growth curves printed right on it, making it easy to track baby's weight during immunization visits.

question: What is the main job of tiny channels called canaliculi in compact bone?

options.A: To house the main blood vessels running down the bone
options.B: To anchor skeletal muscles securely to the bone surface
options.C: To connect bone cells so they can share food and waste
options.D: To produce new red blood cells in the bone marrow

explanation: Well done! Because the bone matrix is hard and blocks direct blood flow, these tiny channels (canaliculi) act like little highways letting bone cells pass nutrients back and forth.

question: Which of these is a key behavioral warning sign that a school-aged child might be at risk?

options.A: Sudden and unexplained drop in academic performance
options.B: Consistent completion of all assigned homework tasks
options.C: Increased enthusiasm for structured extracurricular sports
options.D: Active participation in school health club meetings

explanation: Well done! A sudden, unexplained crash in grades usually means a child is dealing with hidden stress, abuse, or negative peer pressure.

question: Why is community conversation so important when trying to stop FGM in local Nigerian settings?

options.A: Traditional leaders have no influence over community behavior
options.B: Local laws forbid nurses from ever talking about reproductive health
options.C: The practice is deeply tied to cultural identity and social acceptance
options.D: Economic penalties are the only proven way to change minds

explanation: Because FGM is rooted in deep traditions and social pressure, laws alone aren't enough—we need community-wide education to change hearts and minds. You've got this!

question: What is 'diagnostic overshadowing' in clinical practice?

options.A: Physical symptoms being incorrectly dismissed as psychological issues
options.B: Family members refusing to accept any medical diagnosis
options.C: A patient receiving two different psychiatric labels at the exact same time
options.D: A clinician forgetting to document the patient's primary complaint

explanation: Overshadowing happens when real physical sickness gets ignored simply because the patient has a mental health history. Always look at the whole person!

question: What is a 'status offense'?

options.A: An act that is illegal only because the person is a minor
options.B: Any offense that results in immediate capital punishment
options.C: A minor traffic violation committed by a licensed driver
options.D: A violent crime committed by an adult against a child

explanation: You're doing great! A status offense is an action that is only breaking the rule because of the offender's young age—like skipping school or running away from home.

question: What is an important duty for a nurse after a client joins a workshop?

options.A: Monitoring if the work stress is affecting the client's mental health
options.B: Manufacturing the goods alongside the clients every afternoon
options.C: Setting the daily market prices for the workshop products
options.D: Managing the financial bank accounts of mulberry farms

explanation: Nurses watch closely for any signs of burnout or relapse to make sure the work remains healing rather than harmful. Proud of your progress!

question: What is the recommended compression rate per minute for adult CPR?

options.A: 60 to 80 compressions per minute
options.B: 140 to 160 compressions per minute
options.C: 100 to 120 compressions per minute
options.D: 40 to 50 compressions per minute

explanation: Aim for a steady, brisk rhythm of 100 to 120 compressions per minute. Fun fact: pumping to the beat of the song 'Stayin' Alive' helps hit this exact speed!

question: When your brain interprets information and decides what to do about it, what is this process called?

options.A: Motor output
options.B: Hormone secretion
options.C: Integration
options.D: Sensory reception

explanation: Think of integration as your brain's processing unit making sense of all the clues it receives. Great job keeping up with your nursing studies! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a healthcare referral pathway?

options.A: To ensure patients never leave their local village clinic
options.B: To punish nurses who cannot solve complex surgical problems
options.C: To connect patients to higher levels of care when needs exceed primary facilities
options.D: To increase the financial profit of private pharmacies

explanation: When a patient's condition is too complex for a primary health post (like needing a C-section or major surgery), a referral pathway ensures they get smoothly transferred to a general hospital.

question: A patient admits they smoke too much, but they have zero plans to quit anytime soon. Which stage of change are they in?

options.A: Preparation
options.B: Maintenance
options.C: Precontemplation
options.D: Contemplation

explanation: In precontemplation, a person isn't ready to change yet and might not even see a problem with their habit. It's our job as nurses to meet them where they are with patience!

question: What is the main characteristic of a nursing team in the performing stage?

options.A: They are preparing to permanently disband the unit
options.B: They constantly argue about who should do shift handovers
options.C: They are just getting to know each other and remain very polite
options.D: They work together smoothly to achieve high-quality care

explanation: In the performing stage, the team operates with high synergy, trust, and efficiency. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h3)

question: Why does long-term low blood oxygen sometimes lead to secondary polycythemia?

options.A: The liver releases clotting factors to repair damaged alveolar walls
options.B: The bone marrow responds to inflammation by producing excess white blood cells
options.C: The body tries to carry more oxygen by making extra red blood cells
options.D: Dehydrated blood vessels concentrate the existing red blood cells rapidly

explanation: You're nailing this! Making extra red blood cells is the body's clever way of packing more oxygen-carriers into the blood when air supply is low. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why do patients on standard chemotherapy often experience hair loss and mouth sores?

options.A: The chemical makeup of the drugs directly dries out the outer layers of human skin.
options.B: The radiation energy absorbed by the bloodstream weakens oral and scalp tissues.
options.C: Patients naturally stop eating enough fresh fruits and vegetables due to nausea.
options.D: The medications attack all rapidly dividing cells, including healthy normal cells like hair follicles and mucosal linings.

explanation: Exactly! Chemotherapy targets fast-growing cells. Sadly, it can't tell the difference between cancer cells and our healthy fast-growing cells, like hair and gut linings.

question: Why do we always push iron and folate supplements during antenatal care?

options.A: To cure existing chronic infections in the uterus
options.B: To increase the total body weight of the mother
options.C: To speed up the physical growth of the mother's hair
options.D: To prevent anemia and neural tube defects in the baby

explanation: Iron keeps the mother's blood strong and fights off tiredness (anemia), while folate protects the baby's developing brain and spine. It's a powerful combo!

question: What important skill do sperm cells pick up while chilling in the epididymis?

options.A: They mix with acidic prostate fluid
options.B: They multiply rapidly through mitosis
options.C: They gain the ability to swim
options.D: They lose their tails completely

explanation: Think of the epididymis as a training ground where immature sperm finally develop motility so they can swim forward.

question: Why is it important for nursing students to understand how healthcare is funded?

options.A: Nurses are directly responsible for collecting hospital revenue
options.B: It explains why some facilities lack basic supplies and equipment
options.C: It is required for writing national health policies
options.D: It determines the specific salary scale for health workers

explanation: You've got this! Knowing where hospital money comes from helps you make sense of the real-world shortages and everyday challenges you will see during clinical postings.

question: What security practice involves giving staff access only to the patient files needed for their specific job duties?

options.A: Role-based access control
options.B: Universal computer sharing
options.C: Open public network browsing
options.D: Manual paper chart locking

explanation: Role-based access limits what parts of an EHR a user can see based on their specific job role, protecting patient privacy. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which of these sources is the most trusted and reliable for an academic literature review?

options.A: Personal diary entries of patients
options.B: Anonymous social media posts
options.C: Peer-reviewed journal articles
options.D: Commercial product advertisements

explanation: Peer-reviewed articles have been checked and approved by other experts in healthcare, making them solid evidence for your study.

question: How do modern nutritional guidelines differ from the ones created in the early 20th century?

options.A: They now focus on preventing chronic diseases in addition to stopping deficiencies
options.B: They have completely removed any guidelines regarding vitamins and minerals
options.C: They only focus on calculating the exact amount of daily calories needed
options.D: They are designed exclusively for treating severe hospital patients

explanation: You got it! While older guidelines just wanted to stop diseases like rickets, today we also look at long-term wellness, like preventing heart disease and obesity.

question: Which management style best reflects the psychology part of Deming's framework?

options.A: Encouraging teamwork, reducing workplace fear, and respecting individual differences
options.B: Assuming staff only care about their end-of-month salary
options.C: Publicly scolding nurses who make minor math errors on drug calculations
options.D: Demanding blind obedience to rigid rules without question

explanation: Great leaders build psychological safety so nurses feel supported, motivated, and confident to do their best work.

question: Where should a completed incident report be submitted in the hospital?

options.A: Pinned to the public notice board in the main nursing station
options.B: Glued permanently inside the front cover of the patient's bedside chart
options.C: Mailed straight to the national nursing council office
options.D: Submitted directly to the quality or risk management department

explanation: That's right! Incident reports go straight to risk management or quality units, keeping them separate from the patient's clinical bedside chart.

question: A nurse recognizes that a specific pattern of lab results points to sepsis. Which level of the informatics continuum does this represent?

options.A: Information
options.B: Data
options.C: Knowledge
options.D: Wisdom

explanation: Knowledge is formed when information is synthesized to recognize patterns and understand relationships, such as connecting lab values to a specific condition. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why doesn't having plenty of food in the country automatically mean everyone is well-nourished?

options.A: Government regulations legally restrict citizens from buying more than basic rations
options.B: Local populations automatically reject imported food items due to personal preferences
options.C: Stored food spoils instantly before it can be transported to local neighborhood markets
options.D: Food may be present in the country but remain unaffordable or inaccessible to poor households

explanation: Just because food is in the country doesn't mean poor families have the money to buy it. Distribution and wealth play huge roles!

question: What should you do if a patient pushes out a suppository right after you insert it?

options.A: Inspect the stool, check the status, and consult the prescriber for a repeat dose
options.B: Immediately force a second suppository into the rectum without checking
options.C: Assume the full dose was already absorbed and document successful administration
options.D: Scold the patient for failing to hold the medication inside the bowel

explanation: If it comes out whole before melting, the dose is lost, and you must check with the prescriber before trying again.

question: Why is it so important to encourage a patient to drink lots of fluids after a bone scan?

options.A: To prevent severe dehydration caused by the strong magnetic fields
options.B: To replace the fluid lost during the mandatory fasting period before the test
options.C: To activate the chemical tracer so it can take clearer pictures of the spine
options.D: To help flush the remaining radioactive tracer out of the body through urine

explanation: Drinking plenty of water helps the kidneys wash out any leftover radioactive tracer quickly, lowering radiation exposure.

question: What is most important for a tele-nurse trying to check a patient's skin rash over a video call?

options.A: Adequate lighting in the patient's room
options.B: The presence of background music
options.C: The brand of the patient's television
options.D: High room temperature

explanation: Good lighting is key! Without it, the camera won't show the true color and texture of the skin.

question: Which of these conditions is NOT typically confused with a benign cervical ectropion during an exam?

options.A: Uterine fibroids located in the myometrium
options.B: Benign cervical polyps protruding from the os
options.C: Early malignant tumors of the cervix
options.D: Cervicitis caused by sexually transmitted organisms

explanation: Fibroids sit deep inside the muscular wall of the uterus, way past the surface of the cervix, so they won't look like a red patch on the outer cervix. You nailed it!

question: How do bacterial efflux pumps help germs beat drugs?

options.A: By blocking white blood cells from entering tissues
options.B: By dissolving the outer layer of human skin cells
options.C: By actively pushing the medication out of the cell
options.D: By creating new vitamins that feed the pathogen

explanation: Think of efflux pumps like tiny security guards that rapidly throw drug molecules right back out before they can harm the microbe!

question: What action should a nurse take immediately if a medication administration error occurs?

options.A: Ask the patient to keep quiet about the mistake
options.B: Hide the empty medicine cup in the trash can
options.C: Wait until the end of the month to see if harm happens
options.D: Report it to the doctor and nurse manager right away

explanation: Immediate reporting ensures the patient gets quick medical evaluation and treatment if an adverse effect develops. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h7)

question: How should a bricklayer doing heavy manual labor in the hot Nigerian sun adjust their diet compared to a desk worker?

options.A: Decrease all food intake to prevent excessive sweating
options.B: Eliminate all carbohydrates to protect joint health
options.C: Rely exclusively on vitamin supplements instead of meals
options.D: Increase total energy and macronutrient intake to match high physical exertion

explanation: Heavy physical work burns through calories fast! They need more energy and macronutrients to keep up with the hard work.

question: Why should you pre-test your IEC materials with a small group before mass printing them?

options.A: To sell the materials to community members to raise funds for the clinic
options.B: To ensure the messages are clear and culturally appropriate before full release
options.C: To satisfy government paperwork requirements without involving the community
options.D: To test the physical strength and durability of the printing paper

explanation: Pre-testing helps you catch confusing words or awkward pictures early, saving you from wasting time and money on materials that won't work.

question: If a ward suddenly sees many more surgical site infections because of a poorly sterilized batch of tools, what kind of variation is this?

options.A: Special cause variation
options.B: Common cause variation
options.C: Standard baseline variation
options.D: Theoretical variation

explanation: This is a special cause variation because it is an unexpected, unusual event caused by a specific problem that needs fixing right away.

question: What is the main purpose of setting up youth-friendly reproductive health clinics in local communities?

options.A: To offer young people a safe, non-judgmental space to access contraception and information
options.B: To track and penalize adolescents who engage in early sexual activity
options.C: To distribute free surgical instruments for home use
options.D: To provide mandatory pregnancy testing for all high school graduates

explanation: Youth-friendly clinics take away the fear of judgment and stigma, making it easy for teenagers to ask questions and get reliable health guidance early on.

question: A head nurse wants to quickly find the average temperature of ten patients without doing manual math. Which tool should she use?

options.A: Email attachment settings
options.B: Excel built-in formulas and functions
options.C: PowerPoint animation effects
options.D: Microsoft Word bulleted lists

explanation: Excel formulas are brilliant for this! They do the heavy lifting and math for you in seconds, saving you time and stress. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h3)

question: When an artificial intelligence alert pops up on a patient monitor, what should the nurse do?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately based on the computer screen
options.B: Ignore the patient completely because the computer is always right
options.C: Turn off all hospital monitors so they stop making noise
options.D: Evaluate the alert and use clinical judgment to decide the next step

explanation: Technology is a support tool, and nurses must always apply their own professional assessment before taking action. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the main difference between curative care and palliative care?

options.A: Palliative care is only used in hospitals, while curative is at home
options.B: Curative care ignores pain, while palliative care uses surgery
options.C: Curative aims to cure disease, while palliative aims to relieve suffering
options.D: Palliative care is only for children, while curative is for adults

explanation: You've got this! Curative care fights to get rid of the illness, while palliative care focuses on making sure the patient is comfortable and free from heavy suffering.

question: Which primary hormone drives the growth of female reproductive organs during puberty?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Testosterone
options.C: Thyroid hormone
options.D: Melatonin

explanation: You nailed it! Estrogen is the main female sex hormone that guides the development of the reproductive system during puberty.

question: Why is having a wide base of support important when standing or lifting?

options.A: It keeps blood flowing to the legs
options.B: It improves overall stability and balance
options.C: It increases the strength of arm muscles
options.D: It stops the patient from feeling dizzy

explanation: A wide base of support, with feet apart, helps keep the body balanced and prevents falls or strains. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h4)

question: What is the function of the coronary arteries that branch off the ascending aorta?

options.A: Carry blood to the upper brain and scalp
options.B: Drain waste products from the lungs
options.C: Connect the aorta to the pulmonary trunk
options.D: Supply oxygen directly to the heart muscle

explanation: The coronary arteries branch off right at the base of the aorta to feed the hardworking muscle tissue of the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h2)

question: What term is used for the time it takes for half of a hormone to be cleared from the bloodstream?

options.A: Degradation time
options.B: Metabolic rate
options.C: Clearance factor
options.D: Half-life

explanation: Just like medicine in the body, a hormone's 'half-life' is simply how long it takes for half of its concentration in the blood to disappear.

question: Why do patients with endocarditis need to take antibiotics for many weeks instead of just a few days?

options.A: Pills take a very long time to reach the stomach
options.B: Heart valves have no blood supply and drugs can't reach them easily
options.C: Bacteria hiding inside valve vegetations are hard for drugs to reach
options.D: Short courses always cause skin allergies

explanation: The clumps of bacteria and platelets (vegetations) don't have their own blood vessels, so it takes a long, steady course of antibiotics to fully wipe them out. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the absolute first priority when managing a severely injured teenager in the emergency unit?

options.A: Securing the airway and stabilizing breathing
options.B: Calling the legal authorities for documentation
options.C: Asking about the history of the quarrel
options.D: Administering long-term psychiatric counseling

explanation: You got it! In emergency trauma care, the primary survey always comes first—focusing on airway, breathing, and circulation to keep the patient alive.

question: Which of the following is an example of demographic data found in an EHR?

options.A: Active blood pressure medication list
options.B: Serum potassium lab test results
options.C: Chest X-ray diagnostic imaging report
options.D: Patient home address and phone number

explanation: Demographics refer to basic personal and contact details rather than clinical test results or treatments. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h2)

question: What factor has the greatest influence on peripheral vascular resistance?

options.A: Total vessel length
options.B: Overall body height
options.C: Vessel radius
options.D: Red blood cell count

explanation: Small changes in vessel radius create exponential changes in resistance, making constriction and dilation the primary way the body controls blood pressure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h6)

question: Who is the main pioneer associated with scientific management theory?

options.A: Florence Nightingale
options.B: Abraham Maslow
options.C: Max Weber
options.D: Frederick Taylor

explanation: Frederick Taylor developed scientific management, focusing heavily on workplace efficiency and time studies. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is accurate handover documentation legally important for you as a nurse?

options.A: It prevents the nursing council from inspecting the hospital
options.B: It serves as evidence that patient care and responsibilities were properly transferred
options.C: It guarantees that the nurse will never be questioned by a doctor
options.D: It allows the hospital to charge higher fees for room maintenance

explanation: Clear notes protect you legally by proving you handed over patient duties responsibly and professionally.

question: How does keeping a food diary differ from doing a 24-hour dietary recall?

options.A: Food diaries measure blood levels instead of food intake
options.B: Food diaries rely entirely on long-term memory
options.C: Food diaries are only performed by specialized surgeons
options.D: Food diaries record items in real-time as they are consumed

explanation: Writing things down as you eat beats trying to remember everything at the end of the day!

question: How can nurse managers prevent staff from feeling overwhelmed by MBO?

options.A: By delegating all objective tracking to external consultants
options.B: By making all goals mandatory and non-negotiable
options.C: By hiding performance data from the nursing staff entirely
options.D: By limiting the number of active goals to a few critical priorities

explanation: Focusing on just a few vital targets keeps the workload manageable alongside bedside nursing duties. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why do doctors order antibody blood tests like rheumatoid factor when checking joint pain?

options.A: To evaluate how well the kidneys filter waste products
options.B: To measure the exact daily amount of calcium in the bones
options.C: To determine if the client has an active bacterial wound infection
options.D: To check for specific proteins that indicate an autoimmune attack

explanation: Tests like rheumatoid factor look for rogue proteins that show the immune system is mistakenly attacking the body's own healthy joint tissues.

question: Why is correct waste segregation at the primary healthcare level so critical?

options.A: It makes the clinic storeroom look neat for visiting supervisors
options.B: It ensures that general waste burns at a much lower temperature
options.C: It protects community waste handlers from accidental injuries and infections
options.D: It allows the clinic to recycle all used plastic syringes into new toys

explanation: Proper sorting ensures that hazardous items like needles and blood-soaked cotton do not end up in municipal dumps where they can harm the public. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of a high calorie diet?

options.A: To lower baseline blood pressure
options.B: To restrict daily sodium intake
options.C: To achieve a positive energy balance
options.D: To speed up digestive transit time

explanation: A high calorie diet is meant to supply more energy than the body burns, creating a positive balance to promote weight gain and healing. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h1)

question: What is the main job of the hypothalamus in your body?

options.A: Maintaining internal balance and homeostasis
options.B: Producing voluntary skeletal muscle movement
options.C: Filtering visual images from the optic nerve
options.D: Processing high-level abstract mathematical thoughts

explanation: Well done! The hypothalamus acts like your body's thermostat and control center, constantly checking temperature, water balance, and chemistry to keep you stable.

question: What is the main job of NEMA and SEMA during emergencies in Nigeria?

options.A: Providing primary school education in displaced persons camps
options.B: Regulating private pharmaceutical prices across the country
options.C: Overall disaster coordination, search, rescue, and relief distribution
options.D: Conducting laboratory tests for infectious disease outbreaks

explanation: NEMA (national) and SEMA (state) are our main government agencies in charge of coordinating rescue and relief when disasters strike.

question: If a displaced community is staying in a crowded makeshift camp after a flood, what health threat should the nurse expect next?

options.A: Immediate reduction in baseline community trauma rates
options.B: Rapid spread of waterborne and communicable diseases
options.C: Sudden widespread outbreaks of genetic blood disorders
options.D: Total elimination of chronic lifestyle health conditions

explanation: When people are crowded together with poor sanitation, infectious diseases can spread very quickly. Nurses play a huge role in preventing this!

question: A patient comes to your clinic with severe watery diarrhea and dehydration after drinking untreated stream water. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: Cholera
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Severe diarrhea and rapid fluid loss after drinking unsafe water are classic signs of a bacterial infection like cholera.

question: What is the single biggest cause of cancer worldwide that we can actually prevent?

options.A: Processed meat intake
options.B: Alcohol consumption
options.C: Ultraviolet radiation
options.D: Tobacco use

explanation: Tobacco smoke contains harmful chemicals that damage our DNA. Avoiding tobacco is one of the best health choices anyone can make!

question: A nurse manager uses a directive approach with a nursing student on day one, but gives more independence by week eight. Which leadership concept does this show?

options.A: Transactional compliance
options.B: Laissez-faire neglect
options.C: Situational leadership
options.D: Autocratic rigidity

explanation: Changing your leadership style as the learner gains confidence and skill is the definition of situational leadership. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h6)

question: Your patient started a new drug and now has yellow eyes, dark urine, and tummy pain on the upper right side. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: A normal, expected side effect of starting antibiotic therapy
options.B: An idiosyncratic liver reaction to the new drug
options.C: An acute kidney injury caused by dehydration
options.D: A simple skin allergy triggered by sunlight

explanation: Yellow eyes (jaundice) and dark urine are classic red flags for drug-induced liver trouble. Great clinical spotting!

question: Why does damage to the pancreas often lead to both digestive problems and blood sugar issues?

options.A: Digestive enzymes and hormones are stored inside the exact same cells.
options.B: Insulin is required to activate all major pancreatic digestive enzymes.
options.C: The pancreas has both exocrine and endocrine functions in one organ.
options.D: The pancreas shares a direct blood supply with the liver and stomach.

explanation: You've got this! The pancreas is a multitasker. It acts as an exocrine gland to help us digest food, and an endocrine gland to manage our blood sugar. When it gets injured, both jobs take a hit.

question: Why is a low white blood cell count (neutropenia) a medical emergency for patients on chemotherapy?

options.A: It prevents the kidneys from filtering normal metabolic waste products
options.B: It leads to severe joint stiffness and sudden hair loss across the scalp
options.C: The body loses its primary defense against invading bacteria and pathogens
options.D: It causes immediate, uncontrollable bleeding from small skin cuts

explanation: Spot on! Neutrophils are our infection-fighting soldiers. When they drop, even minor germs can quickly cause serious infections.

question: A nurse wants to lower catheter-related infections in the surgical ward. Following research principles, what should be done first?

options.A: Stop using catheters entirely for every single surgical patient
options.B: Review current research for evidence-based catheter care guidelines
options.C: Wait for patient complaints before changing the cleaning routine
options.D: Punish staff members who report high infection numbers

explanation: Spot on! Whenever we want to solve a clinical problem, checking current research helps us find safe, proven protocols that actually work.

question: What is one of the most common challenges faced by PTAs in executing health projects?

options.A: Lack of children attending the primary schools
options.B: Financial constraints and inability of parents to pay levies
options.C: Excessive funding from international health organizations
options.D: Too many doctors volunteering to work in schools
