options.C: It contains active cells, blood vessels, and nerves that respond to the body's needs
options.D: It grows larger only by absorbing water from the surrounding skin tissues

explanation: You got this! Bones aren't just dead sticks; they are packed with blood and nerves so they can repair themselves and react to stress.

question: Which healthcare professional helps residents recover their ability to do everyday tasks like dressing and bathing?

options.A: Pharmacy delivery
options.B: Occupational therapy
options.C: Wound debridement
options.D: Intravenous therapy

explanation: Occupational therapy helps patients regain everyday self-care skills so they can live as independently as possible. Keep up the great work!

question: What usually happens to a patient when their pancreas stops making enough digestive enzymes?

options.A: Malabsorption and nutritional deficiencies
options.B: Severe dehydration from excessive water retention
options.C: Widespread hardening of the intestinal walls
options.D: Rapid weight gain due to unchecked fat storage

explanation: Without enough enzymes, food passes through without being properly broken down, meaning the body misses out on vital nutrients and vitamins. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h7)

question: Which of these details must you include when charting AROM exercises?

options.A: The personal phone number of the patient's family
options.B: The brand name of the bed sheets used in the room
options.C: The specific joints exercised and the number of repetitions
options.D: The exact cost of the physical therapy equipment

explanation: Good documentation means noting down exactly which joints you worked on and how many times they moved.

question: Which complication can occur if a patient fails to rinse their mouth after using an inhaled corticosteroid?

options.A: Sudden closure of the vocal cords
options.B: Severe inflammation of the esophagus
options.C: Oral fungal infection or thrush
options.D: Permanent discoloration of the teeth

explanation: Residual steroid powder left in the oral cavity alters normal flora, frequently causing fungal overgrowth known as oral thrush. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the name for an organism like a mosquito that transmits a pathogen to a human?

options.A: Capsid
options.B: Dermatophyte
options.C: Vector
options.D: Mycelium

explanation: Vectors carry infectious agents from an infected animal or person to a new host. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h4)

question: When helping a stroke patient with left-sided weakness put on a button-down shirt, which arm goes in first?

options.A: Whichever arm the patient prefers
options.B: The left arm
options.C: The right arm
options.D: Both arms at the same time

explanation: Always dress the weak (affected) side first! It makes maneuvering the fabric much easier before the strong arm is tucked in.

question: What is the best feeding item to use when giving ORS to an infant?

options.A: A clean cup and spoon
options.B: A rubber feeding bottle
options.C: A wide-spout drinking straw
options.D: A plastic syringe with a needle

explanation: Always choose a clean cup and spoon! Baby bottles have narrow parts that are very hard to clean properly and can easily trap germs that cause more infections.

question: Why is a pregnant teenager at a much higher risk for nutritional shortages than an adult pregnant woman?

options.A: She is still growing herself and must compete with the fetus for nutrients.
options.B: Adult women require half the daily calories of teenagers.
options.C: Her digestive tract is shorter and absorbs fewer vitamins overall.
options.D: Hormones during teen pregnancy completely block fat digestion.

explanation: Correct! The teen's body is still finishing its own growth spurt while also feeding a growing baby, creating a huge demand for extra nutrients.

question: What major risk must nurses watch out for when patients take long-term immunosuppressant drugs?

options.A: Rapid and permanent weight loss
options.B: Increased susceptibility to severe opportunistic infections
options.C: Total loss of taste and smell
options.D: Excessively high blood pressure caused by thickened blood

explanation: When we quiet the immune system to stop it from attacking the body, it also struggles to fight off normal germs. Good patient education on hygiene is key here!

question: Why must nurses adjust their teaching style when educating patients about blood health?

options.A: To prove that modern medicine is superior to local traditions
options.B: To match the patient's literacy level and cultural background
options.C: To make the education session finish much faster
options.D: To ensure the medical terms are as complex as possible

explanation: Clear, culturally sensitive communication ensures patients truly understand how to protect their health and follow prevention guidelines. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of an emergency preparedness plan in home births?

options.A: To make sure the birth happens without any pain medication
options.B: To prevent dangerous delays in reaching a hospital during complications
options.C: To guarantee that the birth takes less than two hours
options.D: To collect gifts from neighbors before the baby arrives

explanation: Having transport, money, and a destination ready saves precious time when an emergency strikes. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h7)

question: What is the antidote used in acute iron poisoning?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Atropine sulfate
options.C: Protamine sulfate
options.D: Deferoxamine

explanation: Deferoxamine acts like a magnet, binding to excess iron in the blood so the kidneys can safely flush it out during an overdose.

question: Why do we use barium sulfate during a barium meal X-ray test?

options.A: To act as a contrast medium on X-rays
options.B: To neutralize excess stomach acid
options.C: To numb the lining of the stomach
options.D: To speed up the digestion of food

explanation: You're doing great! Barium coats the inside of the gut and blocks X-rays so we can see the organs clearly on the screen. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h1)

question: Even though a benign tumor is non-cancerous, why can it still be dangerous to a patient?

options.A: It always releases toxic poisons into the bloodstream
options.B: It can press on vital structures inside confined spaces
options.C: It frequently turns into widespread blood cancer
options.D: It destroys the immune system completely

explanation: Think about a crowded room! Even if things are peaceful, if a tumor grows inside a tight space like the skull, it can press on vital organs and cause serious trouble.

question: You notice a mother's partograph has crossed the alert line at a primary health centre. What is your best next step?

options.A: Administer large doses of unprescribed herbal concoctions
options.B: Arrange for prompt transfer to a facility with comprehensive emergency obstetric care
options.C: Stop all monitoring and advise the mother to sleep until morning
options.D: Discharge the patient home with instructions to walk around more

explanation: When the alert line is crossed at a primary center, it's time to arrange a safe transfer to a higher hospital before things reach the action line.

question: A patient with an enlarged prostate hasn't peed in eight hours and has severe lower belly pain. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink more water to flush the system
options.B: Administer a mild oral water pill (diuretic)
options.C: Prepare equipment for urinary catheterisation as ordered
options.D: Apply a warm compress to the lower back and wait two hours

explanation: Great thinking! When urine gets trapped because of an enlarged prostate, getting it out with a catheter right away relieves the painful pressure.

question: What is the standard lab test used to find intestinal parasite eggs and cysts?

options.A: Stool microscopy
options.B: Skin patch testing
options.C: Urinalysis dipstick
options.D: Chest X-ray imaging

explanation: Makes total sense! Since intestinal parasites live in the gut, checking a stool sample under a microscope is the quickest way to spot their eggs or larvae.

question: What is the protective protein coat that surrounds the genetic material of a virus called?

options.A: Flagellum
options.B: Cellulose wall
options.C: Capsid
options.D: Peptidoglycan

explanation: The capsid acts like a tough little armor shell protecting the virus's genetic code from the outside world.

question: Which type of joint is known for having a fluid-filled space between the bones?

options.A: Fibrous joint
options.B: Suture joint
options.C: Cartilaginous joint
options.D: Synovial joint

explanation: Well done! Synovial joints are special because they have a fluid-filled cavity that keeps the bone surfaces separated and moving smoothly.

question: What is the main use of a run chart in quality improvement?

options.A: To record patient medical diagnoses in an emergency
options.B: To schedule holiday shifts for nurses
options.C: To display data points over time and track performance trends
options.D: To calculate annual salaries for hospital staff

explanation: Spot on! Run charts plot data chronologically so you can see at a glance whether your ward's new interventions are actually improving things.

question: Why can relying only on 'the way we've always done it' (clinical tradition) be tricky in healthcare?

options.A: It prevents nurses from communicating effectively with doctors
options.B: It causes immediate legal action against the hospital management
options.C: It automatically increases the cost of purchasing hospital equipment
options.D: It can keep outdated habits alive that no longer serve the patient well

explanation: Great job! Just because we've 'always done it that way' doesn't mean it's still the best way. Science and care methods keep improving for our patients' benefit.

question: Which of these is NOT a method of environmental vector control?

options.A: Spraying heavy doses of chemical aerosols inside every home
options.B: Clearing stagnant water pools around residential areas
options.C: Cutting away overgrown bushes near houses
options.D: Improving local waste disposal systems

explanation: Spraying chemicals is 'chemical control,' whereas cleaning up bushes, trash, and water pools is 'environmental control' because you're changing their natural habitat.

question: How does a sincere clinical apology usually affect an injured patient or their family?

options.A: It legally bars them from ever asking questions about the incident
options.B: It makes them completely forget that an adverse event occurred
options.C: It validates their suffering and often reduces feelings of anger
options.D: It forces them to discharge themselves from the hospital immediately

explanation: A respectful, honest apology lets patients know their pain is recognized. This often calms their anger and lowers the desire for aggressive lawsuits.

question: What is the main feature of Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI) schemes?

options.A: They require patients to pay the full cost of surgery upfront
options.B: They are funded exclusively by international pharmaceutical companies
options.C: They are voluntary schemes where members pay regular local premiums
options.D: They are mandatory taxes collected by the federal government

explanation: CBHI relies on people within the community choosing to chip in regularly so they can share medical risks together. Simple and effective!

question: Which ventilator mode gives a full machine breath whenever the patient tries to breathe, plus a backup rate just in case?

options.A: Assist-Control
options.B: Spontaneous breathing
options.C: Control Mode
options.D: SIMV

explanation: In Assist-Control mode, the machine is right there helping. Every time the patient initiates a breath, the ventilator steps in to deliver a full breath, and a backup rate ensures they never miss one.

question: Why is it dangerous to stuff a sharps box until it is completely filled to the brim?

options.A: It increases the risk of needle stick injuries for anyone handling the box.
options.B: It makes the container too heavy to lift.
options.C: It prevents the waste from being incinerated properly.
options.D: It causes the plastic walls to dissolve chemically.

explanation: When a sharps box is overstuffed, needles poke out of the top. Anyone trying to close or carry the box risks getting painfully stuck!

question: A nurse throws an empty IV fluid bag with no blood stains into the regular office bin. Is this okay?

options.A: Yes, because it is general non-hazardous waste
options.B: No, intravenous items are always treated as sharps
options.C: No, all plastic items must go into infectious bins
options.D: Yes, provided the bag is shredded first by the nurse

explanation: Great choice! Clean packaging and IV bags that haven't touched blood or body fluids are safe to go into the general waste bin.

question: Why is it recommended to start a PDSA test with just one patient or one nurse?

options.A: Patients refuse to let more than one nurse care for them
options.B: It guarantees that no data will ever need to be collected
options.C: It minimizes risk and makes it easy to adjust the idea if something goes wrong
options.D: Hospital regulations forbid testing on more than one person at a time

explanation: Great thinking! Starting microscopically small keeps patients safe and prevents staff burnout while you work out the kinks.

question: Who is usually the first member of the nursing team to notice small, daily changes in a resident's condition?

options.A: Director of nursing
options.B: Billing administrator
options.C: Facility pharmacist
options.D: Certified nursing assistant

explanation: Certified nursing assistants (CNAs) spend the most time with residents, making them amazing at spotting early signs of a change in health!

question: A patient with an enlarged prostate is most likely to experience which problem?

options.A: Complete inability to produce testosterone
options.B: Permanent loss of the sense of thirst
options.C: Severe pain during the production of new sperm
options.D: Difficulty starting and maintaining a urine stream

explanation: Because the prostate surrounds the urethra, swelling or enlargement pinches the tube and obstructs urine flow. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h3)

question: What does the term 'nutrient density' really mean for healthy eating?

options.A: Consuming meals that contain only fat and carbohydrate sources
options.B: Choosing foods with the longest possible shelf-life in the pantry
options.C: Getting the highest amount of vitamins and minerals per calorie of food
options.D: Eating foods that weigh as much as possible to fill the stomach

explanation: You're doing great! Nutrient density is all about getting the most nutritional bang for your buck—maximum vitamins with a sensible calorie count.

question: How often are hospital policies typically scheduled for review and updating?

options.A: Every two to three years
options.B: Every twenty to thirty years
options.C: Only after a major court case occurs
options.D: Every single week without fail

explanation: Policies are checked every few years to keep up with new medical evidence, changing laws, and real feedback from the wards.

question: How long must symptoms of ODD be present to meet standard diagnostic criteria?

options.A: More than five years
options.B: At least two weeks
options.C: At least six months
options.D: Exactly one month

explanation: Diagnostic manuals require a duration of at least six months of persistent irritable and defiant behavior for an ODD diagnosis. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T1#GNS314_U2_T1_h2)

question: How do local disaster teams handle poor or flooded roads during an emergency?

options.A: By waiting months until the floodwaters dry up completely
options.B: By demanding that heavy trucks drive through flooded bridges anyway
options.C: by halting all relief distribution until federal contractors fix the roads
options.D: By utilizing alternative transport methods like local boats, canoes, and motorcycles

explanation: Well done! When big trucks can't pass, using local boats, canoes, or bikes is a smart way to get supplies to people who are cut off.

question: Which of these is NOT a common bottleneck when trying to control government health spending?

options.A: Bureaucratic inefficiency and delayed fund releases
options.B: Weak accounting systems leading to resource leakage
options.C: Immediate and transparent tracking of every kobo at the clinic level
options.D: Political interference in siting capital projects

explanation: Real-time tracking of every kobo is the ideal goal we want to achieve, not a bottleneck. Weak accounting and delays are the actual problems!

question: Who should you use standard precautions for in the ward?

options.A: All patients receiving care regardless of diagnosis
options.B: Visitors and administrative staff members only
options.C: Patients admitted specifically to isolation wards
options.D: Only patients with confirmed infectious diseases

explanation: Great job! Standard precautions are meant for EVERY patient, every single time. Since we don't always know who might be carrying an infection, treating everyone with these safety rules keeps both you and your patients safe.

question: What structure is compromised when a rectovaginal fistula forms?

options.A: The anovaginal septum
options.B: The inguinal ligament
options.C: The ureterovesical junction
options.D: The internal cervical os

explanation: The fistula forms when the partition or septum separating the rectum and vagina is damaged or breached. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: Why do growing pituitary tumors often cause vision changes like trouble seeing out of the sides of your eyes?

options.A: Not having enough thyroid hormone causes the retina to wear out quickly.
options.B: Too much growth hormone makes the muscles around the eyeballs swell.
options.C: High pressure inside the skull damages the back part of the brain directly.
options.D: The growing mass presses upward directly against the optic chiasm.

explanation: Location is everything! The optic chiasm (where your eye nerves cross) sits right above the pituitary gland. When the gland swells up, it bumps right into those nerves.

question: How full should a waste bag be before you tie it up and remove it from the ward?

options.A: Whenever the shift ends
options.B: Three-quarters full
options.C: Completely packed to the brim
options.D: One-quarter full

explanation: Brilliant! We tie and remove bags at three-quarters full so there's enough room to close them safely without tearing or spilling.

question: How do educators officially define true "learning"?

options.A: A permanent change in behavior or knowledge from experience
options.B: Attending all scheduled classroom lectures and clinicals
options.C: Memorizing facts for a nursing board examination
options.D: The physical growth of the brain during young adulthood

explanation: Learning isn't just about growing older or cramming for a test—it's when your actual knowledge or actions shift because of real experiences. You've got this!

question: A pregnant patient asks if she can safely drink fresh, unpasteurized goat milk. What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Yes, as long as the goat appears healthy and clean
options.B: No, because raw milk may contain dangerous Listeria or Brucella
options.C: No, but only because raw milk causes severe lactose intolerance
options.D: Yes, because goat milk naturally lacks all human pathogens

explanation: You're doing great! Pregnant women should always avoid raw milk because it can harbor nasty infections like Listeria and Brucella that harm both mother and baby.

question: How do electronic records make a nurse's daily work easier compared to old paper charts?

options.A: By shortening the required length of a hospital stay for surgery
options.B: By eliminating the need to ever measure patient vital signs
options.C: By reducing medication errors caused by poor handwriting
options.D: By removing all documentation duties from the nursing staff

explanation: Great job! We've all struggled to read messy handwriting. Digital records clear that up so nobody gives the wrong drug by mistake.

question: When is an 'organic' organisational structure most helpful to use?

options.A: When managers want complete centralized control over all staff
options.B: In a dynamic, fast-changing environment requiring innovation
options.C: In a strictly regulated factory with repetitive routine tasks
options.D: When communication must strictly follow top-down channels

explanation: Organic structures are flexible and adaptable. They work best in fast-paced settings where teams need to think on their feet and innovate.

question: What happens when a primary health clinic consistently submits its monthly data late?

options.A: It automatically increases the clinic's monthly financial budget
options.B: It creates national data gaps and delays commodity distribution planning
options.C: It exempts the facility from ever doing physical stock counts again
options.D: It transfers the nursing staff immediately to a federal teaching hospital

explanation: Spot on! When reports are delayed at the facility level, the central authorities miss the data they need to distribute drugs properly nationwide.

question: Why is it tricky to study things like pain and fatigue in patients?

options.A: They only occur in male patients
options.B: They are abstract and hard to define uniformly
options.C: They never change over the course of an illness
options.D: They cannot be recorded on any medical chart

explanation: Exactly! Pain and fatigue look and feel different to every single person, which makes them harder to measure the same way every time.

question: Why do you need the patient's muscle to be relaxed before giving an IM injection?

options.A: It prevents the needle from bending inside the skin
options.B: It stops local bleeding from tiny blood vessels
options.C: It makes insertion easier and decreases pain
options.D: It speeds up the chemical breakdown of the drug

explanation: Exactly! A relaxed muscle lets the needle slide in smoothly, while a tense muscle makes it hurt more. A calm patient is a happy patient!

question: Why is true, informed consent impossible when dealing with early or forced marriages involving minors?

options.A: Government laws automatically invalidate all youth marriages
options.B: Minors lack the developmental maturity to fully grasp lifelong consequences
options.C: Families rarely hold traditional wedding ceremonies for youths
options.D: Religious leaders always forbid young people from marrying

explanation: Spot on! True consent means fully understanding a major life decision. Young minds are still developing and cannot grasp these lifelong impacts yet.

question: Why does a drop in local currency value make medications so much more expensive?

options.A: Doctors start prescribing more expensive brands
options.B: Governments place heavy taxes on local pharmacies
options.C: Many essential drugs and raw materials are imported
options.D: Local factories stop producing tablets entirely

explanation: Spot on! Because we import a lot of our medicines and raw ingredients, a weaker currency means it costs much more to bring them into the country.

question: A patient admitted for severe hyperemesis is about to receive IV glucose fluids. Why must she receive thiamine (Vitamin B1) first?

options.A: To help the liver process the incoming sugar more quickly
options.B: To prevent Wernicke's encephalopathy from vitamin deficiency
options.C: To prevent allergic reactions to the plastic IV tubing
options.D: To stop the patient from feeling sleepy during the infusion

explanation: Great catch! Giving sugar to a malnourished patient without thiamine can trigger a serious brain complication called Wernicke's encephalopathy. Always protect the brain first!

question: Who stays ultimately responsible for public health when a government enters into a healthcare PPP?

options.A: The private contracting company
options.B: The international donor organizations
options.C: The government health agency
options.D: The individual hospital nursing directors

explanation: Even if private companies help run things, the government remains the main captain and holds the legal and moral duty for the public's health.

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended first step when managing challenging behaviors in dementia?

options.A: Immediate prescription of heavy antipsychotic medications
options.B: Reviewing the daily routine for sources of overstimulation
options.C: Playing soft and familiar background music
options.D: Looking for signs of physical pain or discomfort

explanation: Always start with non-drug approaches! Heavy meds carry serious risks and shouldn't be the first resort for everyday behavioral issues.

question: Why is nurse advocacy so important when it comes to disability and public policies?

options.A: To help enforce equal rights, accessibility, and reduce societal stigma
options.B: To stop families from caring for relatives at home
options.C: To replace the work of legal professionals in courtrooms
options.D: To secure direct political appointments for hospital administrators

explanation: You are a voice for your patients! Advocating for good policies ensures that people living with disabilities get fair treatment, access, and respect everywhere.

question: Why do qualitative researchers include direct quotes from participants in their results?

options.A: To let participants speak in their own voices and add authenticity
options.B: To replace the need for any written interpretation or analysis
options.C: To increase the total word count of the research report
options.D: To prove that every participant agreed with the researcher

explanation: Verbatim quotes provide direct evidence of the lived experiences, making the qualitative narrative believable and grounded in reality. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h5)

question: How long is the standard course of multi-drug therapy for a patient with multibacillary leprosy?

options.A: Exactly 6 months
options.B: 6 weeks
options.C: 3 to 5 years
options.D: 12 to 24 months

explanation: Multibacillary cases require a longer treatment duration, usually lasting 12 to 24 months, to clear the higher bacterial load. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why would a cell decide to do receptor downregulation?

options.A: To help absorb more nutrients directly from the bloodstream
options.B: To protect itself from being overstimulated by high hormone levels
options.C: To prepare the cell to divide into two identical daughter cells
options.D: To allow fat-soluble hormones to cross the cell wall faster

explanation: If there's way too much hormone around for too long, the cell pulls some receptors inside to take a break and avoid getting overwhelmed. Smart cells know their limits! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h2)

question: What are the three main tiers of the Nigerian health system?

options.A: Local, state, and federal hospitals
options.B: Community, general, and teaching units
options.C: Primary, secondary, and tertiary care
options.D: Private, public, and missionary clinics

explanation: Spot on! Nigeria's health system is broken into three simple levels (primary, secondary, and tertiary) to make sure healthcare reaches everyone from local villages to big cities.

question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse must do when caring for a patient who has overdosed on drugs?

options.A: Maintaining airway, breathing, and circulation
options.B: Discussing long-term career goals and ambitions
options.C: Asking about their family background and history
options.D: Administering a harsh disciplinary warning

explanation: ABC comes first in every emergency! Keeping the patient breathing and stable is always the top priority.

question: A clinic spends its limited budget on new vaccines instead of fixing a leaking roof. What is the opportunity cost here?

options.A: The total financial value of the newly purchased vaccines
options.B: The electricity used to power the vaccine storage refrigerator
options.C: The salary paid to the clinic manager for making the choice
options.D: The protection and comfort lost from delaying the roof repair

explanation: Since they chose vaccines, the opportunity cost is the benefit they missed out on by leaving the roof unfixed for now.

question: What is the normal resting pulse rate for a healthy adult?

options.A: 60 to 100 beats per minute
options.B: 40 to 60 beats per minute
options.C: 100 to 140 beats per minute
options.D: 80 to 120 beats per minute

explanation: A normal adult heart rate at rest falls safely between 60 and 100 beats per minute. Keep this number handy for your ward practice! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is an example of a macronutrient that the body needs in large amounts?

options.A: Trace minerals
options.B: Iron supplements
options.C: Vitamins
options.D: Carbohydrates

explanation: Correct! 'Macro' means big—carbs, proteins, and fats are the big-ticket items our bodies need daily in large quantities for fuel.

question: Why is pre-training essential for nurses who will use research checklists on the ward?

options.A: To teach them how to perform advanced surgical operations
options.B: To make sure they spend less than one minute on each patient
options.C: To prevent the hospital from hiring outside research assistants
options.D: To ensure everyone interprets and records items in the same way

explanation: Training gets everyone on the same page, ensuring your data stays reliable no matter who fills out the form.

question: Why is an individual patient's infection report important to the bigger picture of surveillance?

options.A: It proves the hospital has poor cleaning standards
options.B: It replaces the need for laboratory testing
options.C: It guarantees that funding will increase for the ward
options.D: It helps public health teams spot community outbreaks early

explanation: Every single case serves as a vital data point that can signal the start of a wider spread of disease. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h1)

question: What is a great way for a manager to boost teamwork between day and night shifts?

options.A: Reduce the total number of staff meetings held throughout the year
options.B: Threaten disciplinary action for anyone who complains about handover
options.C: Increase documentation requirements to track intershift communication
options.D: Implement a peer recognition program where staff nominate each other

explanation: Shouting out your colleagues for doing a great job builds friendship and breaks down walls between shifts.

question: Why must nurses know that a normal pregnant woman can have a high white blood cell count?

options.A: To determine the correct dose of routine iron supplements
options.B: To avoid misinterpreting a normal pregnancy change as a severe infection
options.C: To calculate the exact date when spontaneous labour will begin
options.D: To prove that the mother's immune system is completely shut down

explanation: Good nursing judgment! Knowing what is normal for pregnancy prevents us from panicking or treating a healthy mum for an infection she doesn't have.

question: What is the primary goal of a descriptive cross-sectional study?

options.A: To follow patients from birth until old age
options.B: To prove that one factor causes another over time
options.C: To show how common a health condition is in a population
options.D: To test the effectiveness of a new surgical tool

explanation: Descriptive studies simply lay out the facts—like how widespread a condition is—without trying to prove cause and effect.

question: Why is independent double-checking required for medications like insulin and heparin?

options.A: They require special refrigeration that only senior nurses can access
options.B: They are very expensive drugs that require strict financial accounting
options.C: They are high-alert drugs that carry a high risk of patient harm if miscalculated
options.D: They lose their potency quickly if not checked by two people

explanation: High-alert medications have a narrow therapeutic window, meaning small calculation errors cause severe adverse events. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h5)

question: A nurse suspects a young househelp brought to the clinic is being trafficked. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Ignore the suspicion since medical staff only treat physical diseases
options.B: Find a way to speak with the child privately away from the adult
options.C: Send the child home and report the incident to the local market union
options.D: Confront the accompanying employer aggressively in the waiting room

explanation: A private chat gives the child a safe environment to share what's happening without fear of punishment from their handler.

question: What is the best advice for a nurse to give a patient who just had a cervical polypectomy?

options.A: Expect heavy bleeding equivalent to a heavy period
options.B: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampons for a short time
options.C: Douching daily is required to prevent local infection
options.D: Remain on complete bed rest for one full week

explanation: Giving the cervix a little break from anything inserted vaginally lets the small surgical site heal up nicely and safely.

question: What does 'precision' measure in an information retrieval search?

options.A: The percentage of articles written by registered nurses
options.B: The proportion of retrieved documents that are actually relevant
options.C: The total number of seconds the computer takes to search
options.D: The exact number of spelling errors found in the abstract

explanation: Precision evaluates how well your search weeded out useless results, telling you what percentage of what you found was truly useful. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h6)

question: What causes skin to become thick, rough, and leathery, a condition we call lichenification?

options.A: A sudden bacterial infection inside a hair follicle
options.B: Rapid accumulation of watery fluid underneath a bulla
options.C: Chronic scratching and rubbing over a long period
options.D: Exposure to intense ultraviolet sunlight without protection

explanation: When a patient keeps scratching the same spot over and over, the skin fights back by getting thick and leathery.

question: Why is it helpful for a nurse to know the virulence of a germ?

options.A: It shows how quickly the hospital laboratory can bill the patient.
options.B: It helps predict how severe the tissue damage and symptoms might be.
options.C: It dictates the patient's visiting hours in the hospital ward.
options.D: It determines the exact room temperature the patient needs.

explanation: Virulence tells us how strong or nasty a germ is. Knowing this helps you anticipate how sick your patient could get so you can plan better care.

question: What is the function of an audit trail in an electronic health record system?

options.A: To measure how fast patients recover from surgical procedures
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of hospital supplies used daily
options.C: To track and record every user who opens, views, or edits a patient file
options.D: To automatically generate monthly nursing staff duty rosters and shifts

explanation: Audit trails record digital footprints, showing precisely who accessed a patient's record and when, which deters unauthorized snooping. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the main ethical goal of triage when a mass disaster happens?

options.A: Saving the most critically ill patient first, regardless of resource consumption.
options.B: Ensuring doctors spend equal amounts of time on every single casualty.
options.C: Providing the greatest good for the greatest number of people using available resources.
options.D: Treating every patient in the exact order they arrived at the hospital.

explanation: Exactly! Disaster triage flips routine care on its head: instead of focusing only on the sickest individual, you focus on saving as many lives as possible with what you have.

question: What is the main goal when a community nurse acts as an advocate for their patients?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations in local clinics
options.B: Financing private hospitals through personal funds
options.C: Enforcing strict legal penalties against sick community members
options.D: Speaking up for vulnerable groups to improve health resources

explanation: You're doing great! Being an advocate means being a voice for people who might not have the power or platform to speak up for their own health needs.

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to manage or reduce sampling issues?

options.A: Using a larger sample size to decrease natural random sampling error
options.B: Employing random selection methods to give every patient an equal chance
options.C: Purposely selecting only wealthy patients to make hospital data look prestigious
options.D: Setting strict inclusion and exclusion criteria to keep participant groups clear

explanation: You got it! Hand-picking a specific group to make things look good introduces terrible bias instead of fixing research problems.

question: How do newborns primarily generate body heat when they are exposed to cold environments?

options.A: Rhythmic skeletal muscle shivering
options.B: Metabolizing brown adipose tissue
options.C: Sweating through specialized skin pores
options.D: Rapid increase in respiratory rate

explanation: Unlike adults, newborns cannot shiver well; instead, they burn special brown fat stores to create and maintain body heat. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h4)

question: Why is community involvement considered essential for the success of school health programmes?

options.A: It completely removes the financial burden from the government
options.B: It ensures that health habits taught in school are reinforced at home
options.C: It gives community leaders the legal power to hire and fire teachers
options.D: It stops students from falling sick during examination periods

explanation: When communities are involved, healthy practices do not stop at the school gate but continue inside the family environment. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h1)

question: A patient on a tight budget wants a cheap, local source of protein. What should you recommend?

options.A: Imported salmon fillets
options.B: Processed energy drinks
options.C: Beans and cowpeas
options.D: Refined white sugar

explanation: Local beans and cowpeas are fantastic, pocket-friendly powerhouses of plant-based protein right here in Nigeria!

question: What is a common resource barrier faced by nurses trying to maintain quality care in Nigeria?

options.A: An excess of trained nurses with no patients to care for
options.B: Too much free time leading to staff boredom
options.C: Having too many modern computers on every ward
options.D: Shortages of basic consumables like gloves and disinfectants

explanation: It's a tough reality, but lacking basic tools like gloves and clean water makes it super hard to maintain standard infection control.

question: What kind of drug property makes it most likely to build up in breast milk for the baby to absorb?

options.A: A long half-life combined with high lipid solubility
options.B: High protein binding capacity in maternal blood
options.C: Water solubility with a very long elimination time
options.D: Complete destruction by the maternal stomach acid

explanation: Drugs that dissolve easily in fat (lipid-soluble) and hang around in the body a long time (long half-life) tend to linger in breast milk.

question: Why are hospitals moving from paper ledgers to digital health records?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for nurses to write narrative notes
options.B: To ensure that patients never have access to their medical history
options.C: To make hospital storage rooms larger and more spacious
options.D: To capture structured data that improves patient care and continuity

explanation: You've got this! Digital systems make it way easier to share clean, organized data so the whole healthcare team stays on the same page.

question: Why is helping clients connect with their community an important part of day and night hospital care?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any ongoing medication
options.B: It reduces stigma and helps clients function within their social environment
options.C: It ensures patients never have to return to their families
options.D: It allows the hospital to discharge staff and save money

explanation: You got it! Keeping clients connected to their communities builds acceptance and supports long-term recovery.

question: A patient with a racing heart and frequent fainting is scheduled for an EPS. What is the main goal?

options.A: To permanently cure high blood pressure using catheter pressure sensors
options.B: To locate the exact electrical pathway causing the abnormal heart rhythm
options.C: To check how well the heart valves open and close during exercise
options.D: To widen narrowed coronary arteries with a small balloon

explanation: Spot on! The goal is pure detective work: tracking down the exact electrical short circuit that's making the heart race.

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for managing long-term inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: The disease progressively impacts multiple body systems and requires diverse expertise
options.B: It eliminates the need for any involvement from family caregivers
options.C: Specialists must take turns prescribing the exact same daily medications
options.D: Hospital regulations mandate that at least five doctors see every patient

explanation: Because these disorders affect physical, cognitive, and nutritional health, experts from various fields must collaborate to manage complex, changing needs. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h6)

question: What is the medical term for uncoordinated, clumsy muscle movements caused by a problem in the cerebellum?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Anosognosia
options.C: Ataxia
options.D: Aphasia

explanation: Ataxia simply means a lack of smooth muscle coordination, resulting in those jerky, unsteady movements we see in cerebellar issues. You're learning core clinical terms like a pro!

question: What is the main purpose of conditioning an ice pack before putting it in a vaccine carrier?

options.A: To prevent freezing and damaging sensitive vaccines
options.B: To melt the ice completely into warm water first
options.C: To make the ice pack lighter for the community health worker
options.D: To freeze the vaccines faster during transport

explanation: Conditioned ice packs have warmed up slightly so they do not cause accidental freezing of liquid vaccines inside the carrier. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h2)

question: Which statutory body is responsible for regulating nursing education and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: Nigerian Medical and Dental Council
options.B: Federal Ministry of Internal Affairs
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: West African Medical Association

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is the sole legal regulatory authority for the nursing profession in the country. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why do nurses check kidney function (like serum creatinine) before starting certain first-line ARVs?

options.A: Drugs like tenofovir can affect renal function and require safe dosing
options.B: It proves whether the patient has active tuberculosis infection
options.C: Good kidney function guarantees the patient will never miss a dose
options.D: Kidney tests tell the nurse how many CD4 cells the patient has left

explanation: You're right! Some drugs like Tenofovir can put stress on the kidneys, so checking baseline labs ensures the medication is completely safe for that patient's body.

question: Where is the best spot to place a sharps container in the treatment room?

options.A: Underneath the sink in the staff breakroom
options.B: Inside a locked storage room down the hall
options.C: High up on a shelf outside patient reach
options.D: As close as possible to where procedures occur

explanation: Having the box right beside you means you never have to walk across the room carrying a used needle.

question: What makes a conceptual framework so useful when you are reading a published nursing study?

options.A: It proves the researcher spent a lot of money on the project
options.B: It lists every single patient who refused to participate
options.C: It makes the study goals and variable relationships instantly clear
options.D: It replaces the abstract and the conclusion sections

explanation: A good diagram or framework gives you a quick snapshot so you can understand the whole study at a single glance.

question: Why do estrogen levels drop heavily as the ovaries age?

options.A: The liver breaks down estrogen faster than normal
options.B: The remaining ovarian follicles become unresponsive to stimulation
options.C: The adrenal glands block the synthesis of steroid hormones
options.D: The pituitary gland stops making gonadotropins entirely

explanation: Since the follicles inside the ovaries are what make estrogen, losing their responsiveness means estrogen levels naturally fall.

question: What do we call the solid, mulberry-like cluster of cells formed during early embryonic travel?

options.A: Pronucleus
options.B: Zygote
options.C: Morula
options.D: Blastocyst

explanation: Spot on! The morula is a solid little cluster of cells that looks a bit like a tiny mulberry as it travels down the tube.

question: How should a nurse handle bed sheets that are stained with blood?

options.A: Handle them with minimal agitation and bag them securely
options.B: Wash them by hand in the patient bathroom sink
options.C: Leave them on the floor until housekeeping arrives
options.D: Shake them out thoroughly to remove loose debris

explanation: You nailed it! Shaking dirty linens sends dust and germs flying everywhere. Roll them up gently and bag them safely!

question: Which of these terms describes multicellular parasitic worms?

options.A: Bacteria
options.B: Helminths
options.C: Ectoparasites
options.D: Protozoa

explanation: Spot on! Helminths are multicellular worms (like tapeworms and roundworms). Protozoa are tiny and single-celled, while ectoparasites hang out on the outside of the skin.

question: Which of these tiny germs cannot survive on its own and must enter a living host cell to multiply?

options.A: A virus
options.B: A bacterium
options.C: A fungus
options.D: A parasite

explanation: Viruses are tiny! They lack the internal machinery to reproduce by themselves, so they have to hijack a living host cell to make copies. You've got this!

question: Which body fluid carries the highest amount of infectious HIV?

options.A: Saliva
options.B: Blood
options.C: Sweat
options.D: Tears

explanation: Spot on! Blood, semen, and vaginal fluids have high viral loads capable of spreading HIV, unlike everyday touch or fluids like sweat and tears. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is the best example of a clear, well-stated objective for an antenatal clinic?

options.A: Do a better job of talking to patients about their nutrition.
options.B: Make all pregnant women much happier with our services.
options.C: Improve general maternal health across the entire community.
options.D: Increase first-trimester booking attendance by 20% in six months.

explanation: Great goals are specific and measurable! This option gives a clear target (20%) and a timeframe (six months) with no guesswork.

question: Why does the baby's head usually rotate internally as it moves down through the pelvis?

options.A: to signal the placenta that it is time to detach from the uterine wall
options.B: to fit the widest part of the head through the widest diameter of the pelvic outlet
options.C: to prevent the umbilical cord from wrapping tightly around the fetal neck
options.D: to decrease the intensity of maternal uterine contractions

explanation: Correct! The pelvis has specific shapes, and the baby rotates to match those contours for a smoother passage through the birth canal.

question: In the standard IMRAD format used for writing research papers, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Methods
options.B: Medication
options.C: Management
options.D: Measurement

explanation: Spot on! IMRAD stands for Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

question: Why must a nurse assess a patient's breathing technique and coordination before handing them an inhaler?

options.A: Assessment ensures the patient will never experience any drug side effects
options.B: All inhalation devices function identically regardless of the patient's skill
options.C: Patients are legally required to pass a written test before treatment
options.D: Different devices require specific breathing maneuvers for the drug to work

explanation: An MDI requires slow, deep breaths with a spacer, while a DPI requires a sharp inhalation, so matching technique is critical. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why do a community diagnosis before starting an IEC campaign?

options.A: Identify the actual health burdens affecting the local population
options.B: Prove that the community lacks basic hygiene practices
options.C: Fulfill administrative paperwork requirements for the local government
options.D: Determine how many nurses are needed for night duty shifts

explanation: You got it! Just like assessing an individual patient before treatment, a community diagnosis helps you find out what health issues are truly troubling the people.

question: What is the primary function of leukocytes in the human body?

options.A: Digesting complex carbohydrates in the gut
options.B: Regulating blood pressure and fluid balance
options.C: Defending the body against foreign invaders
options.D: Transporting oxygen to body tissues

explanation: Leukocytes are white blood cells whose main job is to recognize and destroy foreign pathogens like bacteria and viruses. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why must the ear pinna be pulled downward and backward for a child under three years old?

options.A: The eardrum sits at a completely different angle in infants
options.B: It prevents the child from turning their head sideways
options.C: Children have more earwax blocking the upper canal
options.D: Their ear canal is shorter and straighter compared to an adult

explanation: An infant's ear canal anatomy requires a downward and backward pull to properly align the passage for drops. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h2)

question: When mistakes happen in the clinic, what is usually the real root cause?

options.A: Flawed system designs interacting with human limits
options.B: Poor physical fitness and lack of sleep
options.C: A lack of basic nursing education among staff
options.D: Intentional negligence by individual healthcare workers

explanation: You're doing great! Remember that most clinical errors happen because the work environment and tools don't properly support natural human limits—not because nurses are careless.

question: Which of these is a modern, digital way to share nursing research?

options.A: Paper memos locked inside a supervisor desk drawer
options.B: Locked institutional archives in university basements
options.C: Professional social media networks and infographics
options.D: Printed textbooks published twenty years ago

explanation: Exactly! Digital tools like social media and colorful infographics help spread useful health tips quickly to a wide audience.

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do when a worker gets a deep cut at work?

options.A: Ask the worker to fill out an insurance claim form first
options.B: Provide immediate first aid and stabilize the worker
options.C: Wait for the company director to arrive and give permission
options.D: Send the worker home without examining the wound

explanation: Always remember your nursing ABCs and emergency priorities—patient safety and immediate first aid come before any paperwork!

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you accidentally get poked by a needle?

options.A: Take a strong dose of broad antibiotics
options.B: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow
options.C: Fill out an incident report form for HR
options.D: Wash the puncture site with soap and water

explanation: Quickly washing the spot with soap and water helps flush away germs before they can enter your bloodstream.

question: A nurse is helping design a public health program to tackle malnutrition in local primary schools. Which type of dietitian should lead this?

options.A: Clinical dietitian
options.B: Renal dietitian
options.C: Surgical dietitian
options.D: Community dietitian

explanation: Community dietitians focus on public health, schools, and larger group or population-wide nutrition programs.

question: What is one of the most common signs of caregiver burnout in family members looking after an aging relative?

options.A: Physical exhaustion and emotional strain
options.B: An immediate surplus of personal free time
options.C: Increased desire to learn complex medical procedures
options.D: Improved sleeping patterns and high energy

explanation: Exactly. Looking after a loved one around the clock without breaks is exhausting, often leading to deep physical tiredness and emotional stress.

question: Why are bedside nurses usually the best people to spot where clinical changes are needed?

options.A: They spend most of their shift working in the hospital administrative offices
options.B: They dictate national health policies and regulatory frameworks
options.C: They have final authority over hospital budget allocations
options.D: They experience daily workflows and spot operational bottlenecks firsthand

explanation: You are right at the bedside every day, so you see firsthand what slows things down or causes delays for patients. Who knows the ward better than you?

question: A patient arrives in the emergency unit after a severe motorcycle crash. According to the ABCDE rule, what should the nurse check first?

options.A: Blood pressure
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Airway patency
options.D: Hidden skin wounds

explanation: Airway is always the top priority in the ABCDE approach because an obstructed airway causes death faster than anything else. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h2)
